title: Numbers 6: Three and Four (same rule, no gender)
titleRussian: Числа 6: три и четыре (то же правило, без рода)
description: Three and four follow the exact rule you learned for two: they reshape the noun into the genitive singular. The relief is that три and четыре have no gender forms - one shape covers every noun.
descriptionRussian: Три и четыре подчиняются тому же правилу, что и 'два': существительное переходит в родительный падеж единственного числа. Хорошая новость — у 'три' и 'четыре' нет родовых форм, одна и та же форма работает с любым существительным.
intro: Three and four ask less of you than two did. They take the same ending on the noun and have no gender forms of their own, so the whole small-number system now fits in a single sentence. Enjoy that while it lasts: from lesson 7 everything above four follows a different rule, and the noun takes a different shape entirely.
rules: Three (три) and four (четыре) take the noun in the genitive singular - exactly like два and две.
Три and четыре have no gender forms. One shape each, regardless of whether the noun is masculine, feminine, or neuter.
The endings you already know apply: masculine consonant + -а; feminine -а switches to -ы (or -и after к / г / х / ж / ш / ч / щ); neuter -о switches to -а; neuter -е switches to -я.
The full 'small numbers' rule now reads: 2, 3, 4 → genitive singular noun. Pick the form of two by gender; three and four are gender-free.
Lesson 7 introduces a completely different rule for the numbers five and above. Today closes the small-numbers chapter.
examples: У Антона три брата. (Anton has three brothers.) Masculine: -а ending on the noun; три does not change.
У Лены три сестры. (Lena has three sisters.) Feminine: -а → -ы; три does not change.
На столе три книги. (There are three books on the table.) Feminine after к: -а → -и.
В доме четыре окна. (There are four windows in the house.) Neuter: -о → -а; четыре does not change.
У меня четыре машины. (I have four cars.) Feminine: -а → -ы; четыре does not change.
На карте четыре моря. (There are four seas on the map.) Neuter soft -е → -я.

The Full 2-3-4 Rule on One Page

items.promptEnglish: Recap from Lessons 4-5: I have two windows.
items.explanation: Recap. Окно is neuter. After 'два' the -о ending changes to -а: окна. Today extends the same rule to три and четыре.
After 'три' the noun stands in the genitive singular, exactly as after 'два': брат → брата. Three has no gender forms, so 'три' stays unchanged regardless of the noun.

items.hint: Feminine -а switches to -ы after 'четыре', same as after 'две'.
items.explanation: Сестра is feminine. -а → -ы: сестры. The word 'четыре' looks the same regardless of gender: one shape, all nouns.

items.promptEnglish: There are three books on the table.
items.hint: Feminine; stem ends in к, so use -и (not -ы).
items.explanation: Книга is feminine, and its stem ends in к. The spelling rule (no -ы after к, г, х, ж, ш, ч, щ) gives -и: книги. Same as in 'две книги' from Lesson 4.

items.promptEnglish: There are four windows in the house.
items.hint: Neuter -о switches to -а after 'четыре', same as after 'два'.
items.explanation: Окно is neuter. -о → -а: окна. Four behaves like two and three: it triggers the genitive singular and stays in one shape itself.

items.promptEnglish: There are three seas on the map.
items.explanation: Море is neuter with a soft -е. -е → -я: моря. The pattern is the same one you saw with 'два моря' in Lesson 5.

blanks: У меня четыре _____. (I have four phones.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Телефон is masculine. After 'четыре' the noun is in the genitive singular: телефон → телефона. Four behaves exactly like two and three for masculine nouns.

errorCorrection.explanation: After три (or четыре), the noun goes into the GENITIVE SINGULAR: кота. The 2-3-4 rule takes the gen sg for any gender.
After четыре, the noun goes into the GENITIVE SINGULAR: места. The 2-3-4 rule applies uniformly across genders.

After три, the noun goes into the genitive singular: подруги (-а → -и after г, by the spelling rule). Note that три has no separate feminine form (unlike два/две); the noun follows the same small-number rule for any gender.

minimalPairs.explanation: The everyday counting form is 'три'. The form 'трое' is a collective numeral used in specific contexts (трое детей, трое суток) and is not the basic counting word taught here.
After 4 the noun is in the genitive singular: сестры. The form сестёр is the genitive plural - it belongs to the next family of rules (5+, Lesson 7).

patternRecognition.question: What ending is added to the word «брат»?
options: no change (the dictionary form is already correct)
patternRecognition.explanation: The word «брат» gains -а: брат → брата. This is the genitive singular ending after the numbers 2, 3, 4.

patternRecognition.question: What ending does the word «окна» have?
patternRecognition.explanation: Окно is neuter. After 'четыре' the -о ending changes to -а: окна. The same move as with 'два окна'.

reviewVocab.definition: small numerals (the informal label for 2, 3, 4; they share one rule - the gen sg on the noun)
reviewVocab.example: К 'малым числительным' относятся 2, 3, 4: после всех трёх существительное стоит в родительном падеже единственного числа.

reviewVocab.definition: shared / gender-free form (три and четыре have a single shape regardless of the noun's gender)
reviewVocab.example: У числительного 'три' нет родовых форм, как у 'два / две': говорим 'три брата', 'три сестры' и 'три окна' — слово 'три' одно и то же.

reviewVocab.definition: the 2-3-4 rule (any of these numbers triggers the genitive singular on the noun)
reviewVocab.example: По правилу 2-3-4 во всех словосочетаниях 'два / три / четыре + существительное' существительное стоит в родительном падеже единственного числа.
